# Touch UI helper glyphs

Helper-footer glyphs for the touch input family, to sit alongside the controller
glyphs (`ctl_ps_*`, `ctl_xb_*`, `ctl_ns_*`) that `ControllerIconGlyph` renders.

Source art, not shipping resources — nothing here is wired up yet. To bundle a
glyph, copy it into `core/core-ui/src/main/res/drawable-nodpi/`.

## Provenance

**Original work**, generated by `gen_touch_icons.py` in this folder. Not from
Zacksly's packs and not derived from them, so nothing here falls under the CC BY
attribution in `../ui-art-credit.txt` — only the visual style is matched.

## Files

| File | Gesture |
| --- | --- |
| `ctl_touch_tap.png` | Tap |
| `ctl_touch_long_press.png` | Long-press |
| `ctl_touch_swipe_up.png` | Swipe up |
| `ctl_touch_swipe_down.png` | Swipe down |
| `ctl_touch_swipe_left.png` | Swipe left |
| `ctl_touch_swipe_right.png` | Swipe right |
| `ctl_touch_swipe_all.png` | Swipe, any direction (sibling of `ctl_*_dpad_all`) |

## Style contract

Measured from the Zacksly packs so the two families read as one system:

- 128×128 PNG, RGBA, straight alpha
- Pure `#FFFFFF` only, transparent ground — no colour, no gradients, no shadow
- 7px stroke, round caps and joins, flat outline/solid-fill mix
- Content bbox ~94–103px, centred (the packs run 86–94px; wide shapes reach 119px)
- Ink coverage 0.13–0.25, matching the packs' 0.13–0.23 band

## Design language

Every glyph shares one element: a solid contact dot at r=17. That is what binds
the set together, and it is why the dot radius is held constant rather than
tuned per glyph.

- **Tap** — dot inside one closed ring: a single instantaneous contact.
- **Long-press** — dot inside two concentric rings: a held, spreading contact.
  Ring count is the only difference from tap, and it stays legible down to 22px.
- **Swipe** — the dot as the touch-down point, a shaft, and a broad solid
  arrowhead. `up` is authored; the other three are exact 90° rotations/mirrors,
  so all four carry identical weight. The arrowhead is deliberately broad — a
  bare arrow reads optically lighter than the 94px-wide glyphs it shares a row
  with.

Swipes deliberately do *not* reuse the d-pad's "cross with one arm filled"
idiom: a swipe is motion, not a button, and touch prompts should be
distinguishable from controller prompts at a glance.

## Known collision

`ctl_touch_tap` is visually close to `ctl_ps_face_east` and `ctl_ns_share`
(both ring-and-ring). Harmless while the footer shows one input family at a
time; if touch and controller prompts can ever appear in the same row, the tap
glyph needs differentiating.

## Regenerating

```bash
python gen_touch_icons.py    # requires Pillow; writes ./touch_icons/
```

Geometry is parameterised at the top of each section (`STROKE`, `RING_R`,
`DOT_R`, arrowhead constants). Shapes are drawn at 6× and downsampled with
Lanczos for clean antialiasing.
